answer.label: A translated statement by
answer.sourceLine: Fidel Castro did declare his Marxist-Leninist commitment in the speech of 2 December 1961. The English translation checked reads “I shall be a Marxist-Leninist to the end of my life”; the searched phrasing is another rendering of that declaration.

author.name: Fidel Castro
author.heading: About Fidel Castro
author.bio: Fidel Castro led the revolutionary movement that overthrew Fulgencio Batista’s government in 1959. He then governed Cuba as prime minister and president, overseeing the consolidation of a one-party communist state and a long confrontation with the United States.

cite.sourceCitation: Castro, Fidel. “Speech on Marxism-Leninism.” 2 December 1961. English translation, Fair Play for Cuba Committee, 1962; transcribed by Marxists Internet Archive.

copyAttribution: Fidel Castro, 2 December 1961 speech; English translation varies. The 1962 text reads “shall ... to the end of my life.”

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The address discusses the formation of an integrated revolutionary party and Castro’s political development. His declaration occurs in an explanation of why he regarded Marxism-Leninism as the appropriate theory for Cuba’s revolution; it is a public political commitment, translated into several English formulations.
